## Mass-conservation regression checks: which test holds which total, to what tolerance (`check_mass`) {#sec-ch13-regression}

### Summary

snapy is meant to conserve mass and, with the right options, energy to round-off. This section lists the tests
that check this, so a user can see which totals are protected and how tightly. For energy, the options are the
gravity-work form and its fixer: @tbl-ch06-conserves-summary (@sec-ch06-conserves) gives, for each form, the
invariant that is exact on a closed column and the logged sum (`ie=` plus `pe=`) to compare. In short: with the
default `gravity-work: face`, the total energy plus the corrected potential energy of @sec-ch06-dwork,
$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ [J], is exact after every stage. `cell` with `gravity-work-fixer` makes
$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ [J], with the discrete potential energy $\mathrm{PE}_d$[^rg-5a69ec7d1978] of @sec-appa, exact after
every step. `cell` without the fixer conserves no total energy.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Indexes the registered tests that assert a conserved total, with their tolerances, and the one log-based mass script.

**Data.** The test sources; for the script, every `mass0=` token of a run's log, @eq-ch13-mass-drift.

**Placement.** Tests under `tests/`; the script runs an example and reads its log afterwards.

**Activation.** ctest for the registered tests; the script is run by hand, since no CMake rule names it.

**Guarantee / limits.** Totals held on small decks to $10^{-12}$ or $10^{-13}$; the script compares only the end points.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch13-regression-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $M_{\mathrm{d},\mathrm{first}}$, $M_{\mathrm{d},\mathrm{last}}$ [kg] the
dry mass of the first and last `mass0=` samples; $\mathrm{drift}$ [-] their relative difference.

Each identity a test asserts is derived in the chapter that owns the operator. The positivity limiter
is @sec-ch08, the moist repairs and the saturation adjustment @sec-ch10, the seams @sec-ch03. This section is the
index: what is held, by which test, and how tightly.

### Derivation

There is nothing new to derive for the registered tests. The log-based script `run_example_mass_check.py` reads
every `mass0=` token of a run's log. It compares the dry mass of the first sample, $M_{\mathrm{d},\mathrm{first}}$
[kg], with that of the last, $M_{\mathrm{d},\mathrm{last}}$ [kg]. The relative drift, a pure number written
$\mathrm{drift}$, must satisfy

$$
\mathrm{drift} = \frac{|M_{\mathrm{d},\mathrm{last}} - M_{\mathrm{d},\mathrm{first}}|}{\max(|M_{\mathrm{d},\mathrm{first}}|, 1)} \le 10^{-8} .
$$ {#eq-ch13-mass-drift}

Its pattern reads one `mass0=` per cycle line, from the block line and the Mesh line alike, and never `masst=`
[check `src/snapy_report/ch13/checks/regression_check.py`, output `regression_check.out`, `[C1]`]. Only the end points
enter, so an excursion of $5\times10^{-6}$ in between passes (`[C2]`). The floor of 1 in the scale makes the test
absolute below a total mass of 1: a $10^{-6}$ relative drift of a mass of $10^{-3}$ passes, while the same drift of
a mass of $10^{3}$ fails (`[C3]`).

Why the script can pass a run that drifted, in three steps:

1. *Only the end points enter.* `check_mass` takes `masses[0]` and `masses[-1]`, so an excursion in between is not
   seen (`[C2]`).
2. *The scale has a floor of 1.* `scale = max(abs(start), 1.0)`, so below a total mass of 1 the test is absolute
   and a large relative drift of a small mass passes (`[C3]`).
3. *The printed digits bound what it can see.* The block line prints 13 decimals and the Mesh line 14, so the
   smallest drift the script can resolve is about $10^{-13}$ relative, far below its default $10^{-8}$.

In the code, @eq-ch13-mass-drift is `check_mass` ({{< code tests/run_example_mass_check.py check_mass >}}).

The registered tests are listed in @tbl-ch13-regression-tests with the tolerance each uses. The float64
tolerance is $10^{-12}$ almost everywhere. It is a round-off margin; none of the tests derives it. The two cubed-sphere limiter tests use $10^{-13}$. The script, its pattern
`MASS_PATTERN` ({{< code tests/run_example_mass_check.py MASS_PATTERN >}}) and its default `--mass-rtol`
({{< code tests/run_example_mass_check.py parse_args >}}) exist at the pin, but the CMake test list does not name the file. So no
ctest checks `mass0=` over a full example run.

### Code

**A minimal input.** The script runs an example and checks its log; it is not registered with ctest. From the
source root of a build at the pin ([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)), with the two-block Straka deck on two
processes:

```bash
python3 tests/run_example_mass_check.py --build-dir build --build-type release \
    --example straka --input straka_proc2.yaml --nproc 2 --backend gloo --mass-rtol 1e-8
```

`--build-type` is the lower-case suffix of the executable (`straka.release`), and `--input` is resolved in
`build/bin`, where the build links the decks of `examples/`. `straka.yaml` would do as well, but it writes a
`pnetcdf` output, which needs a build configured with `-DPNETCDF=ON`; without it the run stops with
"Output type 'pnetcdf' requires PNETCDF[^rg-2954facee0c1]=ON".

**What is refused, and why.** The script raises when the executable or the input deck is missing, when `torchrun`
is missing for more than one process, when the log holds fewer than two `mass0=` samples (no drift can be formed),
and when the drift exceeds `--mass-rtol`; `--backend` accepts only `gloo` and `ucx`
({{< code tests/run_example_mass_check.py parse_args >}}; {{< code tests/run_example_mass_check.py check_mass >}}).

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch13-mass-drift** ({{< code tests/run_example_mass_check.py check_mass >}}):

```python
start = masses[0]
end = masses[-1]
scale = max(abs(start), 1.0)
rel = abs(end - start) / scale          # drift
if rel > rtol:
    raise ValueError(f"Mass drift {rel:.3e} exceeds tolerance {rtol:.3e}")
```

| samples | {{< code tests/run_example_mass_check.py load_masses >}} | `load_masses` | |

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
No registered test checks `mass0=` over a full example run. The only such check is a script that no CMake rule
calls, and it compares only the first and last samples.
:::

1. **Unit tests, not runs.** The registered tests hold their totals on small decks over a few steps. Long-run
   conservation of a production deck is not tested.
2. **Absolute below 1.** The script's floor of 1 makes it absolute for small total masses (`[C3]`).
3. **Gravity budget.** The $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ budget of the gravity-work fixer and its test are part
   of @sec-ch13-fixgrav.
4. **Untested combinations.** The switch combinations that a test exercises are listed in @sec-ch12-matrix.
